description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/principal.rs:213-217 and notification.rs:109-113 validate every destroy[] element is a JSON string and return JmapError::invalid_arguments at the top level if any element is non-string. A naive impl would skip non-string entries silently and produce a 'normal' /set response with only the string entries processed — which would be a quiet client-side compatibility break (clients receiving 'destroyed: [valid_id]' when they passed [valid_id, 123] would not know 123 was ignored).

Why this should be defended: a contributor optimizing the loop might say 'just filter to .as_str() and skip non-strings — RFC 8620 §5.3 doesn't explicitly require the top-level error'. That argument loses on three points:
  1. RFC 8620 §5.3 says destroy is an Id[] (a JSON array of Id strings). A non-string element is a malformed request.
  2. Silent-skip on malformed input is the workspace's catch-all anti-pattern — preserve-unknown applies to ADDITIVE fields, not to type violations on existing fields.
  3. The error message includes the offending value (format!('destroy: every element must be a string Id; got {bad}')) which is actionable for clients debugging request construction.

Test coverage: principal.rs:367-376 (set_destroy_non_string_element_returns_invalid_arguments) and notification.rs:309-319 (set_destroy_null_element_returns_invalid_arguments).
notes: Existing design defended — no code change needed. The destroy-array non-string-element invalidArguments enforcement remains at the top level in both /set handlers, with the inline RFC 8620 §5.3 citation preserved through the .30 refactor (which changed the validation shape from find-then-iterate to single-pass collect-then-iterate without changing the semantic: any non-string element produces a top-level invalidArguments error, never silent skip). Tests set_destroy_non_string_element_returns_invalid_arguments and set_destroy_null_element_returns_invalid_arguments lock it in.
title: Destroy-array non-string element returns top-level invalidArguments, not silent skip
